jeffrey-de-la-torre.text: On May 11, 2026, voted yes on Resolution 2025/26-38, which put a proposal on the November ballot to limit HLPUSD board members to two consecutive four-year terms. It passed 3-2 (Serrano, De La Torre, Quiñones aye; Loera, Kwok no).

source.title: HLPUSD Board Resolution No. 2025/26-38 proposing board term limits (adopted May 11, 2026), as filed with LA County Board of Supervisors

jeffrey-de-la-torre.text: In his district board profile: "I am committed to supporting students, families, educators, and our staff through equity, innovation, and lifelong learning," and to "fostering a collaborative and inclusive educational environment."

source.title: Hacienda La Puente USD: Board of Education member profiles

jessica-rubio.text: Campaign priority on district property: "Explore green space, recreation, education, and community-serving uses before private development."

source.title: Jessica Rubio for HLPUSD School Board campaign site (2026)

jessica-rubio.text: Campaign priority: "Clear, understandable budgets. Strong safeguards against waste, fraud, and misuse."

source.title: Jessica Rubio for HLPUSD School Board campaign site (2026)

jessica-rubio.text: Campaign priority: "Demand timely testing, full transparency, and immediate action when environmental hazards threaten our schools."

source.title: Jessica Rubio for HLPUSD School Board campaign site (2026)

jessica-rubio.text: Campaign priorities include strengthening "staffing, services, and support for students with disabilities and their families" and ensuring the community is "heard before major decisions."

source.title: Jessica Rubio for HLPUSD School Board campaign site (2026)
